facts.statement: Laplatasaurus is a titanosaurian sauropod named after La Plata, Argentina, whose only known specimen was found in the Anacleto Formation.
facts.quote: Laplatasaurus (meaning "La Plata lizard", named for La Plata, Argentina) is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in South America, with the holotype and only known specimen found in the Anacleto Formation.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene named the genus Laplatasaurus in 1927, but it remained a nomen nudum because it lacked a formal description.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1927 by Friedrich von Huene, but without a description, so that it remained a nomen nudum.

facts.statement: Huene formally described the type species Laplatasaurus araukanicus in 1929.
facts.quote: In 1929 the type species, Laplatasaurus araukanicus, was described by Huene.

facts.statement: Huene based Laplatasaurus on fragmentary fossils from three locations in the Campanian-age Anacleto Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Huene based Laplatasaurus on fragmentary material found in three locations in Argentina, in strata of the Anacleto Formation, dating from the Campanian faunal stage.

facts.statement: José Fernando Bonaparte selected a tibia and fibula (MLP 26-306) as the lectotype in 1979, though they may come from different individuals.
facts.quote: Huene never assigned a holotype, but in 1979 José Fernando Bonaparte chose MLP 26-306 as the lectotype, a specimen consisting of a tibia and a fibula that perhaps originate from different individuals.

facts.statement: Laplatasaurus was approximately 18 meters long and may have been similar in build to Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: The about 18 m long Laplatasaurus was perhaps similar to Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: Huene described Laplatasaurus as a large yet elegantly built sauropod.
facts.quote: Huene asignó esos fósiles a Laplatasaurus que parecía indicar un saurópodo bastante grande pero al mismo tiempo elegantemente construido.

facts.statement: Laplatasaurus measured approximately 18 meters in length with an estimated weight of 30 tonnes.
facts.quote: Laplatasaurus medía aproximadamente 18 metros de largo, teniendo un peso estimado de 30 toneladas.

facts.statement: The tibia and fibula of Laplatasaurus are gracile and slender, distinguishing them from those of Titanosaurus and partially from Antarctosaurus.
facts.quote: La tibia y la fíbula son características, siendo gráciles y delgadas rasgos que los distinguen claramente de los de Titanosaurus y parcialmente de Antarctosaurus.

facts.statement: The leg bones of Laplatasaurus are 50 percent larger than those of Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: Estos son un 50 por ciento más grande que las de Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: The specimens are significant as they represent the first report of armor on a sauropod.
facts.quote: La importancia de los especímenes es que representa el primer informe de la armadura en un saurópodo.

facts.statement: Osteoderms forming a armored plating on the back have been referred to Laplatasaurus, but this association is uncertain.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos que forman un revestimiento blindado en la parte posterior se han referido a Laplatasaurus, pero la asociación es incierta.

facts.statement: The osteoderm plates on Laplatasaurus had much smaller ridges than those found on Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: Estas placas tenían crestas mucho más pequeñas que las de Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: No cranial material was found; the collection includes two presacral vertebrae, twenty caudal vertebrae (ten articulated), limb elements, shoulder girdle material, and some juvenile material.
facts.quote: No se encontró ningún material del cráneo, sólo dos vértebras presacrales y veinte caudales, diez de ellas articuladas, material de los miembros y de la cintura escapular, así como un poco de material juvenil para ir con los miembros.

facts.statement: Huene never assigned a holotype, but Bonaparte and Gasparini selected a tibia and perone as the type for L. araukanicus in 1979.
facts.quote: Huene nunca asignó un holotipo, J. F. Bonaparte y Zulma Gasparini en 1979 seleccionaron una tibia y un peroné como el tipo de L. araukanicus.

facts.statement: Numerous additional specimens were found at the same location and at Rancho de Ávila in Los Alamitos, Río Negro.
facts.quote: Aparte de estos numerosos ejemplares fueron encontrados, en especial de la misma localización y en el Rancho de Ávila en Los Alamitos, Río Negro.

facts.statement: Laplatasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Laplatasaurus araukanicus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Laplatasaurus es un género de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Laplatasaurus lived from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Huene classified Laplatasaurus in the family Titanosauridae, a classification that remains common.
facts.quote: Huene placed Laplatasaurus in the Titanosauridae, which is still a common classification.

facts.statement: A 2015 assessment found Laplatasaurus closely related to Bonitasaura, Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus, and Uberabatitan.
facts.quote: A 2015 re-assessment of Laplatasaurus found it to be closely related to Bonitasaura, Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus, and Uberabatitan.

facts.statement: A 2015 evaluation found Laplatasaurus closely related to Bonitasaura, Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus, and Uberabatitan.
facts.quote: Una nueva evaluación de 2015 de Laplatasaurus encontró que estaba estrechamente relacionado con Bonitasaura, Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus y Uberabatitan.

facts.statement: It is debated whether all material assigned to L. araukanicus belongs to the same genus and species or to unknown forms, due to incomplete associated material.
facts.quote: Sin embargo aclaran que un problema difícil a resolver, con tantos descubrimientos pero sin tener un material asociado suficientemente completo, es difícil saber si la totalidad de material asignada a L. araukanicus corresponden al mismo género y especie, o si corresponde a las formas no conocidas en el presente.

facts.statement: A Megaloolithus egg found in the Anacleto Formation may have been laid by Laplatasaurus rather than Titanosaurus.
facts.quote: A Megaloolithus egg found in the Anacleto Formation in Auca Mahuevo, Argentina that was once assigned to Titanosaurus may have instead been laid by Laplatasaurus.
